heading: INT. THE BRANDT HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT

units.text: INT. THE BRANDT HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
The power cut hit forty minutes ago.
A single candle gutters on the granite island.
Rain runs down the dark windows.
Somewhere in the neighbourhood, a generator coughs and gives up.
Colleen Brandt, 50s, still in her work lanyard, stands at the counter with a bottle of wine she can't open without light.
Her husband's boss's wife has not yet arrived.
Her son's Xbox sits uselessly on the table.
Walter Pryce, 40s, in a damp suit, comes in from the garage with a flashlight.
You're late.
units.name: COLLEEN

units.text: There's a tree down on Maple. I walked.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: In those shoes.
units.name: COLLEEN

units.text: In these shoes.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: He sets the flashlight on its end.
It throws a pale circle at the ceiling.
The refrigerator hums for a moment, then dies with a sigh.
Rain.
I want to say something and I want you to let me finish.
units.name: COLLEEN

units.text: Okay.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Twenty-two years at Halvorsen. I trained every one of those people upstairs. I wrote the manual they pretend to follow. Last Thursday they put me in a room and a boy named Tyler, who is twenty-nine, told me my role was "being reimagined." He used the word "journey." He said I had been on a journey.
units.name: COLLEEN

units.text: Colleen...
units.name: WALTER

units.text: I'm not finished. I smiled. I thanked him. I went to my desk and I alphabetised the supply cupboard because I did not know what else to do with my hands. And then I came home and made a lasagna that nobody ate, because the power went, and that's the whole of it.
units.name: COLLEEN

units.text: The candle gutters.
She finally puts the wine down.
This is the last evening either of them will pretend the house is fine.
I got the same email.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Colleen turns.
For the first time, she looks at him.
